assessment: A solid, self-auditing scan: it caught and reran a rate-limited run that had produced false 'empty repo' data, reports the four required categories separately, and cites repo-level identifiers plus two real script defects; but it does not serve the DEUS position strategy at all (no price thresholds, xDEUS/cooling logic, escrow flow, or any actionable alert), it ends up long rather than 'decide-in-one-glance', and most numeric claims (coverage percentages, 96/79/250 counts, star and commit figures for unlisted repos) come without per-repo queries or measurement timestamps, so only partial verification is possible.
